Field Viewer - first-time user instructions

Extract the application, select a Petrel project, then open the report and recovered data.

Red outline rectangles mark the fields, buttons and information to use. Screenshot paths are examples; use your own folders.

GitHub: Project repository · Download the Windows package · Release notes and downloads

1. Extract the ZIP 2. Choose the application folder 3. Check your project files 4. Open Field Viewer 5. Enter the full .pet path 6. Choose the output and options 7. Wait for the final result 8. Open the HTML report 9. Read the status and gaps 10. Check QC and metadata 11. Open the extracted files 12. Find outputs by category 13. Inspect data with its metadata
Step 1 of 13

Extract the ZIP

You need Windows 64-bit, the complete application ZIP, a complete Petrel project and enough free storage for the outputs. Python and Petrel do not need to be installed separately. The screenshots use the SLB 2018 demo; use your own project path.

  1. In File Explorer, select the downloaded Field Viewer ZIP. Click Extract all.
  2. Extract the whole ZIP. Do not run the launcher from inside the compressed folder.
Step 2 of 13

Choose the application folder

  1. Enter a short, writable destination, for example C:\FieldViewer. Use a new folder if an earlier version is already present.
  2. Leave Show extracted files when complete checked. Click Extract.
Step 3 of 13

Check your project files

  1. Keep the .pet file beside its matching .ptd folder. Include every subfolder and seismic file.
  2. Keep any other supplied project folders with the project. Use a copy and preserve the original files.
Step 4 of 13

Open Field Viewer

  1. In the extracted application folder, double-click FieldViewer_data_extractor (the Windows batch file). Windows may hide the .bat extension.
  2. Keep the launcher beside the FieldViewer folder. Wait while the bundled runtime is prepared and checked.
Step 5 of 13

Enter the full .pet path

  1. At Full path to the .pet project or .zgy file, paste the complete .pet path, including the filename. Press Enter.
  2. Use the location on your own computer. The example below is the demo path shown in the screenshot.

Demo example - replace this with your own full project path:

C:\FVTest\Input\SLB_DEMO_2018\Petrel2010 demo project_2018.pet
Step 6 of 13

Choose the output and options

  1. At Output root, enter a short folder outside the source project, then press Enter. Example: C:\FVTest\Results\MyProject.
  2. At Convert supported data as well?, press Enter for Yes. At Calculate full seismic SHA-256?, press Enter for Yes.
  3. The full report and inventory are always included. Keep the console open while extraction runs.
Step 7 of 13

Wait for the final result

  1. Wait until the final status and output paths appear. Large projects can take a long time; allow the current run to finish.
  2. Completed with gaps means outputs are available with stated limitations. Read the report before using them. Exit 10 by itself is not an installation failure.
  3. After the final result and support ZIP are shown, press Enter to close the console. If the status is Failed, retain the logs and support ZIP and investigate before retrying.
Step 8 of 13

Open the HTML report

  1. Open the output folder you chose. Double-click the file ending in _REPORT.html. Windows may display it without the extension.
  2. You can also open OPEN_RESULTS. Keep the report beside its _EXPORTS and _data folders so the links work.
Step 9 of 13

Read the status and gaps

  1. Read Run status and the category outcome table. Check what was recovered and what has missing or unsupported metadata.
  2. Click Readable diagnostic summary for details when a category is partial. A completed run does not mean every object was decoded.
Step 10 of 13

Check QC and metadata

  1. Click QC & evidence in the report. Read the warnings and open the relevant evidence links.
  2. Before importing a file, check its units, CRS and seismic axes in the matching metadata.json.
Step 11 of 13

Open the extracted files

  1. Click Extracted files in the report. Read the unit and recovery-status columns for the objects you need.
  2. Click Open EXPORTS folder to browse the outputs. Use Download file index (CSV) to get the file list.
  3. Keep data files with their metadata sidecars. Read unresolved-unit notices before using an export.
Step 12 of 13

Find outputs by category

  1. In _EXPORTS, open the category you need, such as logs, grids or seismic.
  2. Open FILE_INDEX.csv for the full accepted file list. Filenames contain object identities to help match data to metadata.
Step 13 of 13

Inspect data with its metadata

  1. Open an exported samples.csv in a text editor or spreadsheet. Check the columns, raw values and null flags.
  2. Open the matching metadata.json. Check unit_status, depth/axis units and crs_status for that object.
Keep the report, _EXPORTS and _data folders together. If you need help, retain the logs and support ZIP; review the archive before sharing it.
